Mi primer mes en Zaragoza / Meu primeiro: Mi primer mes en Zaragoza / My first month in Zaragoza
Faz um mês que moro em Zaragoza. Quando: I've been living in Zaragoza for a month. When I arrived it was raining and I was very tired, but a work colleague was waiting for me at the station. Since then I've worked in an office in the centre and I live in a small flat near the tram. At first I didn't know anyone. Now I have several friends and we meet up almost every weekend. Yesterday we went to the cinema, and the film we saw was very funny. Tomorrow I have a doctor's appointment, because my back has hurt for a week. If all goes well, I'll stay here two years and I'll learn to cook better than my neighbour.

Os 20 erros mais comuns do A2: The 20 most common A2 mistakes for English speakers
Leia cada par em voz alta: primeiro o er: Read each pair out loud: first the wrong one, then the right one. This list is the answer key to the most frequent traps for English speakers — most come from translating English tenses, prepositions and word order literally. Tick the ones you've made and repeat them during the week.
With «ayer», a finished time: indefinido (even though British English can say "I've been").
O radical de «hacer» no indefinido é «hi: The stem of «hacer» in the indefinido is «hic-».
A person as direct object takes «a» (English has nothing like it).
The comparative of «bueno» is «mejor» (no "more good", like English "better").
Plans: «ir a» + infinitive — don't drop the «a» ("going TO buy").
After «si», use the present — as in English "if I HAVE time", never "if I will have".
With «usted», the imperative swaps the vowel.
Thanks: «gracias por» — English "thanks FOR" is «por», not «para».
No stranded preposition: not "the house I live IN" — use «donde» or «en la que».
Verbo no plural e artigo, não possessivo: Plural verb and the article, not the possessive (not "my feet hurt" word for word).
"For two years" is «desde hace dos años».
